summary: E: drive (Samsung SSD 980 PRO 1TB, FW 5B2QGXA7, \Device\RaidPort2, PCI\VEN_144D&DEV_A80A) experienced an NVMe controller lockup/drop at 2026-11-04 18:51:10 local time (23:51:10 UTC) under simultaneous C++/MSBuild compilation (E:\B174, E:\T174, P109) and VSS/encrypted backup coordinator I/O.

windows_event_log_evidence.message: The driver detected a controller error on \Device\RaidPort2.
Failure status: A device which does not exist was specified. VolumeId: E:, Device model: Samsung SSD 980 PRO 1TB, Firmware: 5B2QGXA7.

historical_health_check: Zero prior stornvme or WHEA-Logger errors in the past 30 days; Wear=0; patched firmware 5B2QGXA7 confirmed.
recommended_recovery: 1. Pause/checkpoint active Codex tasks on C: so no new E: writes are attempted while \Device\RaidPort2 is offline.
2. Perform a full Windows Shutdown (NOT a warm Restart), wait 15-20 seconds for the motherboard 3.3V M.2 rail to discharge so the Samsung Elpis NVMe controller resets, then power back on.
3. After boot, run chkdsk E: /scan (read-only online scan) to verify NTFS journal replay on E:\B174, E:\T174, and coordinator_preparation before resuming P109 builds and E: backup.
4. Avoid running heavy multi-process MSBuild compilations on E: concurrently with full-drive VSS shadow / backup hashing on E:.
